correctness.rationale: The simplex-integral formula gives the exact tagged-isolation split; conditioned endpoint pairs rescale to independent ordinary interval graphs on each side; the factorial-weight recurrence controls mixed-side probability to \(1/(2n)+O(n^{-2})\). Exact edge-indicator covariance follows from overlap probability 2/3 on each side and a strictly positive cross-side correction. Boundary dominated convergence gives \(n^2p_n\to1\) and \(n^4C_n\to1/2\), hence covariance \(-2/3\). Exhaustive rational checks through six intervals agree but do not substitute for the analytic argument.

value.rationale: Isolated intervals are a natural obstruction to connectivity; an exact Palm decomposition of the whole remainder graph gives a reusable fragmentation mixture for arbitrary labeled subgraph statistics. The \(O(n^{-1})\) TV concentration gives a useful sharp-scale structural approximation, while the finite negative edge covariance converges to a nonzero constant despite the isolate count vanishing in probability. This is an intrinsically motivated property of the classical random interval graph, not a numerical parameter slice.
